dominant_cause.pinned_mechanism: In T665, modifying services.jar inside system.img changed classes2.dex CRC32 from 0xfa0310b9 to 0xdf90e1bc, which invalidated the precompiled ART boot profile signatures (boot-image.prof / cache-info.xml). At boot, odrefresh detected the profile checksum mismatch, exited with code 79 (kCompilationRequired), and invoked dex2oat64 to recompile the boot classpath into /data/misc/apexdata/com.android.art/dalvik-cache/arm64/. When ZygoteInit started, ART loaded the newly compiled boot artifacts, causing ZygoteInit to crash with SIGSEGV (SEGV_MAPERR, fault addr 0x0) in art::ArtField::GetDeclaringClass (#04 boot-framework.oat ZygoteInit.main+2164) before system_server could launch. The underlying wall from T665 (UserDataPreparer failing on tmpfs /data because Linux 4.19 lacks shmem_user_xattr_handler for user.* xattrs) must therefore be solved at the filesystem layer without modifying services.jar or any boot-classpath JAR: mounting an ext4 filesystem on /data natively supports user.* xattrs. Os.getxattr(path, 'user.serial') returns ENODATA (errno 61) instead of ENOTSUP (errno 95). UserDataPreparer.getSerialNumber natively catches ENODATA and returns -1, and enforceSerialNumber calls setSerialNumber which succeeds without entering the recovery reboot wipe path. The four paths checked by enforceSerialNumber (/data/user/0, /data/user_de/0, /data/system_de/0, /data/system_ce/0) all reside on /data and are 100% covered by the ext4 mount.

candidate_filesystem_layer_ext4_mount.evidence: On ext4, user.* xattrs are natively supported (fs/ext4/xattr.c). Unset xattr returns ENODATA. UserDataPreparer.java:349 catches ENODATA and returns -1. enforceSerialNumber(:299) logs 'Serial number missing ...; assuming current is valid' and calls setSerialNumber(:349), which succeeds on ext4 without throwing IOException. The wipe path is avoided natively without altering system.img.

candidate_checked_paths_scope.evidence: UserDataPreparer.enforceSerialNumber checks exactly 4 paths: getDataUserDeDirectory (/data/user_de/0), getDataSystemDeDirectory (/data/system_de/0), getDataUserCeDirectory (/data/user/0), and getDataSystemCeDirectory (/data/system_ce/0). All four are subdirectories of /data; mounting ext4 on /data natively provides ext4 semantics for all four.
